headline: Composio has no managed Shopify app, so you always bring your own: an app for your own store (or one bespoke client store) is self-serve and same-day, but letting many merchants connect requires a public app that passes Shopify App Store review, runs embedded in the Shopify admin, starts installs from Shopify instead of a typed store name, and gets protected customer data approval for Composio's default customer and order scopes.

notes: OAuth is per store: each merchant authorizes at https://{store}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize, so you need the store's myshopify name before the flow can start.
There is no Admin API discovery document and no dynamic client registration. A store's /.well-known/openid-configuration describes the Customer Account API (buyer login), not the Admin API.
New apps are created in the Dev Dashboard (dev.shopify.com) or with Shopify CLI. Apps created directly in the Shopify admin can no longer be created; existing ones keep working.

Public apps must use expiring offline tokens (1-hour access token, 90-day refresh token) for GraphQL Admin API calls. New public apps already can't use non-expiring tokens; existing public apps lose them on 1 January 2027. Custom and merchant-created apps are exempt.
Apps acting only on stores in your own organisation can use the client credentials grant instead (no redirect, 24-hour tokens). Composio exposes this as S2S auth.

paths.label: Your own store (app in your store's organisation)
paths.summary: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard opened from your own Shopify admin. There is no distribution choice and no review, and custom apps get protected customer data by default. Only stores in your own organisation can install it.

start_here.action: In your Shopify admin open Settings > Apps > Develop apps > Build apps in Dev Dashboard, and create the app there.
Release a version with Composio's scopes and redirect URI, then install it on your store from the Installs card.
Connect through Composio with your store's myshopify name (the 'acme' in acme.myshopify.com).

paths.label: One client's store (custom distribution)
paths.summary: Build the app in your Partner organisation and choose Custom distribution: an install link for one merchant (or the stores in one Shopify Plus organisation), with no review. Shopify's terms allow a custom app for a single merchant only, and Shopify staff say copying the same app for each merchant to avoid review breaks the Partner Program Agreement.

badges.text: Needs a Shopify Partner organisation: the Distribution card only appears for apps that belong to one.
Shopify's API Terms require a privacy policy and a merchant agreement for custom apps too.
One merchant per app (or the stores in one Shopify Plus organisation).
The store owner installs the app from the install link you send.

start_here.action: Create the app in your Partner organisation's Dev Dashboard and release a version with the scopes and redirect URI.
Choose Custom distribution (permanent), generate an install link for the client's myshopify domain and send it to the store owner.
Once installed, connect through Composio with the client's store name.

paths.label: Many merchants (public app, Shopify App Store review)
paths.summary: The only allowed way to let many merchants connect. Choose Public distribution, register for the App Store (US$19 once), build an embedded admin UI, request protected customer data access, and pass App Store review. You can keep the listing at limited visibility, but the review still applies.

gates.title: Protected customer data access (Level 2: name, email, phone, address)
gates.trigger: Composio's default scopes for customers, orders, draft orders, fulfillment orders and gift cards reach protected customer data. On real stores a public app gets those fields only after Shopify approves its request.
gates.avoid: Drop the customer, order, draft order, fulfillment order and gift card scopes if the agent doesn't need them (Level 0), or ask only for Level 1 data without the name, email, phone and address fields.

gates.title: Shopify App Store review (app and listing)
gates.trigger: Choosing Public distribution. Until the app passes review it installs only on dev stores, and every approved public app has an App Store listing, even at limited visibility.

wait.note: Shopify publishes no review timeline and staff say they can't give one. Community-reported: about 2 weeks is typical in October 2026; developers reported waits of around 2 months earlier in 2026.

badges.text: One-time, non-refundable US$19 App Store registration per Partner account.
Needs a Shopify Partner organisation to select Public distribution.
A privacy policy and merchant agreement are required; reviewers check the privacy policy.
Before approval the app installs only on dev stores created in the Dev Dashboard.
Public apps must use expiring offline tokens: 1-hour access tokens and 90-day refresh tokens.

start_here.action: Create the app in your Partner organisation, choose Public distribution, and pay the US$19 App Store registration.
Meanwhile build and test on a dev store from the Dev Dashboard; protected customer data works there without review.
Build the embedded admin page that starts the Composio connection with the shop name Shopify passes on install, add compliance webhooks, and file the protected customer data request.
Submit for review, then don't resubmit or withdraw while queued.

scopes.what: Products, variants and collections. Not protected customer data.
Create and edit products, variants and collections (includes read).
Orders from the last 60 days. Orders are protected customer data: public apps need approval; custom apps get it by default.
Edit, cancel and close orders (last 60 days). Protected customer data, as read_orders.
Customer records. Level 2 protected data when name, email, phone or address fields are used; review for public apps only.
Create and edit customers. Same protected customer data rules as read_customers.
Inventory items and levels.
Adjust inventory levels.
Fulfillment services (FulfillmentService). Fulfilment records on orders come through the order scopes.
Register and edit fulfillment services.
Fulfillment orders assigned to your app's locations. Shipping and fulfilment data tied to a customer's order is protected customer data.
Act on fulfillment orders assigned to your app. Same protected data rules.
Pages, blogs, articles and comments. Shopify says store comments carry customer data, so commenter details are redacted for unapproved public apps.
Edit pages, blogs, articles and comments. Same rule for commenter details.
Read themes and theme files.
Theme changes. Modifying theme files through the Admin API also needs an exemption from Shopify; theme app extensions don't.
Store locations.
Carrier services. Shopify lists shipping rates tied to a single order as protected data; unclear whether this scope alone triggers the request.
Create and edit carrier services. Same uncertainty as read_shipping.
Gift cards. Gift cards used by a single customer are protected customer data.
Issue and edit gift cards. Same protected data rule.
Script tags on the storefront.
Add and remove storefront script tags.
Marketing events and activities.
Create marketing events.
Price rules (legacy discount model).
Create and edit price rules.
Automatic and code discounts.
Create and edit discounts.
Draft orders. Protected customer data: public apps need approval.
Create and complete draft orders. Same protected data rule.
Metaobject entries.
Create and edit metaobject entries.
Not found in Shopify's GraphQL or REST access scope references (checked 2026-10-20). Unclear whether Shopify ignores or rejects it.

Which sales channels products and collections are published to.

prerequisites.item: Owner or staff access with app development permissions on your Shopify store
prerequisites.why: The own-store app lives in your store's organisation, and only users with app development permissions can create it.
The Distribution card (custom or public) only appears for apps that belong to a Partner organisation.

prerequisites.item: A dev store created from the Dev Dashboard (Dev stores > create)
prerequisites.why: Unreviewed public apps install only on dev stores, and protected customer data needs no review there.

prerequisites.item: A public privacy policy and a merchant agreement
prerequisites.why: Shopify's API Terms require both for public and custom apps, and App Store reviewers check the privacy policy.

prerequisites.item: An HTTPS app server you run (embedded admin page and compliance webhook endpoints)
prerequisites.why: App Store apps must be embedded in the Shopify admin with App Bridge and subscribe to compliance webhooks; Composio does not host these for you.

prerequisites.item: Each merchant's permanent myshopify.com store name
prerequisites.why: Composio needs it to build the store's OAuth URL; it is the 'acme' in acme.myshopify.com, not a custom domain.

prerequisites.item: Merchant consent before using store data to train or fine-tune AI models
prerequisites.why: Shopify's API Terms forbid using API or merchant data to train or improve AI models without Shopify's or the merchant's consent.

steps.title: Open the Dev Dashboard in the right organisation
steps.detail: Own store: in your Shopify admin go to Settings > Apps > Develop apps (or search 'App development') and click 'Build apps in Dev Dashboard'; the app then belongs to your store's organisation. Client or public app: sign in with your Shopify Partner account and open the Dev Dashboard for your Partner organisation. Pick carefully: installs without a distribution method, and the client credentials grant, only work for stores in the same organisation.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: In the Dev Dashboard go to Apps > Create app > Start from Dev Dashboard, name the app and click Create. For an App Store app Shopify recommends scaffolding with Shopify CLI instead, because it needs an embedded UI; the client ID and secret work the same way.

steps.title: Declare the scopes in a version
steps.detail: On the app's Versions page, enter the scopes. Use the same list as the scopes field of your Composio auth config, so the merchant approves exactly what the agent uses. Remove what you don't need: on a public app, every customer, order, draft order, fulfillment order and gift card scope brings protected customer data review. read_webhooks and write_webhooks are not in Shopify's scope reference; remove them if the release or install rejects them.

paste.label: Smaller set without protected customer data (catalogue, inventory, discounts)

steps.title: Set the App URL and redirect URI, then release
steps.detail: In the same version set the App URL (a non-embedded app can use Shopify's default below; a public app uses your embedded app's URL) and add the redirect URI. It must exactly match the redirect URI set in your Composio auth config. If you leave the auth config's redirect field at the toolkit default, register the legacy https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add instead. Then click Release.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret
steps.detail: Open the app's App settings in the Dev Dashboard and copy the Client ID and Client secret. Keep the secret out of code and chat logs.

steps.title: Install on your store and test the connection
steps.detail: On the app's Home click Install app on the Installs card and approve the scopes. Then connect through Composio with your store name (the 'acme' in acme.myshopify.com), not your custom domain. When you add scopes later, release a new version and run Install app again so the grant updates.

steps.title: Choose Custom distribution and send the install link
steps.detail: On the app's Home, Distribution card > Select distribution method > Custom distribution, then confirm. This cannot be changed later. Enter the client's myshopify.com or admin.shopify.com domain, keep 'Allow multi-store installs for one Plus organization' only if they are on Plus, click Generate link and send it to the store owner. Build one app per client for that client's needs; Shopify staff say duplicating the same app per merchant to avoid review breaks the Partner Program Agreement.

steps.title: Register for the Shopify App Store (US$19)
steps.detail: Partner Dashboard > Settings > App Store registration > Register now, add a payment method and click Register. One-time and non-refundable per Partner account. Link any associated developer accounts while registering.

steps.title: Choose Public distribution
steps.detail: On the app's Home, Distribution card > Select distribution method > Public distribution, then confirm. This cannot be changed later. If you keep separate dev and production apps, choose it on the production app. The card then links to 'Manage Shopify App Store listing'.

steps.title: Build the embedded app shell Shopify requires
steps.detail: App Store apps must run embedded in the Shopify admin with App Bridge, start installation from Shopify (never ask the merchant to type a store domain), authenticate with OAuth right after install, use only the GraphQL Admin API and subscribe to Shopify's compliance webhooks. Composio's hosted connect form asks for the store name, so start the Composio connection from your embedded page with the shop name Shopify sends on install already filled in, and use Composio's GraphQL tools rather than its legacy REST actions. Our estimate: about two working days.

steps.title: Request protected customer data access
steps.detail: Do this before you submit; you can't apply while the app is under review. Open the request form from the App Store review page (or Apps > your app > API access requests > Protected customer data access > Request access). Select protected customer data with a reason, then only the fields you need (name, email, phone, address) with a reason each, and complete the Data protection details. Ask for the minimum: Shopify approves only what the app needs.

paste.label: Reason: protected customer data
paste.value: Our AI assistant acts for the merchant on the merchant's own orders and customers, only when the merchant asks it to (for example: look up an order, update a customer's tags, create a draft order). We process this data only to complete the merchant's request, do not sell or share it, keep it only as long as the task needs, and encrypt it in transit and at rest.

paste.label: Reason: name and email fields
paste.value: The merchant asks the assistant to find customers and orders by name or email, and the assistant shows who an order belongs to. We do not use these fields for marketing or to train AI models.

steps.title: Complete configuration and the App Store listing
steps.detail: On the App Store review page finish the configuration (app URLs without the word 'Shopify', a 1200 x 1200 icon, API contact email and an emergency developer contact) and create at least one listing with your privacy policy and pricing. After approval you can set the listing to limited visibility so it stays out of search; the review is the same either way.

steps.title: Record the demo screencast and prepare test access
steps.detail: Record a screencast in English (or with English subtitles) that walks step by step through install, onboarding, the Composio connection and each core feature. Add working test credentials for any login your app needs and keep them valid for the whole review.

steps.title: Run the checks and submit for review
steps.detail: Run the automated checks on the App Store review page and the AI self-review, fix what they flag, then click Submit your app. Watch for email from noreply@shopify.com and the review dashboard under App > Distribution. Don't resubmit or withdraw while queued: that moves you to the back of the queue.

while_you_wait.text: Build and test against a dev store created in the Dev Dashboard: draft public apps install there, and protected customer data works without a review request.
Keep test credentials and the demo store working the whole time; reviewers pause when they hit a login wall, and pushing a new version mid-review is reported to restart things.
Use only Composio's GraphQL-based Shopify tools while building, so nothing depends on the legacy REST API that new public apps may not use.
There is no review wait on this path: once the store owner installs the app, you can connect and work immediately.

blockers.symptom: Installing on a client's store fails with "This app can’t be installed on this store. [App name] can only be installed on stores that are part of the same organization."
blockers.cause: The app lives in your Partner organisation and the client's store doesn't. Without a distribution method, apps install only inside your own organisation.
blockers.fix_now: Select Custom distribution on the app's Distribution card, generate an install link for the client's store and send it to the store owner.
blockers.fix_properly: Decide distribution before you build, because it can't be changed: custom for one bespoke client, public for many merchants.

escalate.how: Post in the Dev Platform category with the app's client ID and the store's myshopify domain.
escalate.draft: Our Dev Dashboard app (client ID: <id>) shows 'can only be installed on stores that are part of the same organization' when installing on <store>.myshopify.com. We selected Custom distribution and generated an install link for this store. What else is needed?

blockers.symptom: Agent calls fail with 403 "This action requires merchant approval for read_orders scope" or ACCESS_DENIED naming a scope.
blockers.cause: The scope isn't in the released version, or the store's grant hasn't been updated since you added it.
blockers.fix_now: Add the scope, release a new version, run Install app (or the install link) again so the merchant approves it, then reconnect the account in Composio.
blockers.fix_properly: Keep the Dev Dashboard scopes and the Composio auth config scopes identical, and check granted scopes (Composio's SHOPIFY_GET_ACCESS_SCOPES tool) before going live.

escalate.how: Post in Authentication & Access and include the x-request-id header from the failing response; Shopify staff ask for it.
escalate.draft: After releasing a version with read_orders and reinstalling, our app still gets 403 'This action requires merchant approval for read_orders scope'. App client ID: <id>, store: <store>.myshopify.com, x-request-id: <id>. Can you check the grant?

blockers.symptom: The Composio connection fails with a 400 error or a redirect error on Shopify's authorize page.
blockers.cause: A wrong client secret, a redirect URI that doesn't exactly match one in the released version, or a requested scope that needs Shopify's approval (the OAuth error reads missing_shopify_permission).
blockers.fix_now: Re-enter the client secret, make the redirect URI in the Dev Dashboard match the Composio auth config exactly, release, and start a fresh connection.
blockers.fix_properly: Request only scopes the app can declare; ask Shopify for approval scopes such as read_all_orders before adding them.

escalate.how: Post in Authentication & Access with the exact error text and the authorize URL (remove the client secret).
escalate.draft: Our app (client ID: <id>) gets '<error text>' at /admin/oauth/authorize with redirect_uri <uri>. The same URI is listed in the released version. What are we missing?

blockers.symptom: On a real store, customer name, email, phone or address come back null with "This app is not approved to access the Customer object."
blockers.cause: A public app without approved protected customer data access. Shopify redacts the fields; dev stores are exempt.
blockers.fix_now: Keep testing on a dev store, and tell pilot merchants these fields stay hidden until approval.
blockers.fix_properly: Request protected customer data and each field with reasons, complete the Data protection details and meet the Level 1 and Level 2 requirements before you submit; you can't apply while under review.

escalate.how: Contact Shopify Partner Support from the Partner Dashboard with the app's client ID.
escalate.draft: Our public app (client ID: <id>) needs protected customer data Level 2 (name, email) for <reason>. The request was submitted on <date>; fields still return 'This app is not approved to access the Customer object'. Can you tell us the status?

blockers.symptom: The app sits in Submitted ('We're assigning a reviewer') for weeks, or testing pauses for days between reviewer sessions.
blockers.cause: Shopify's review backlog: staff say review times are longer than usual and give no timeframe. Reviewers also stop when test credentials or the demo store don't work.
blockers.fix_now: Don't withdraw or resubmit; that sends you to the back of the queue. Check the review dashboard under App > Distribution and your email for questions, and make sure test access works.
blockers.fix_properly: Run the AI self-review and the automated checks until clean before you submit, so you pass in one round.

escalate.how: Reply on the flagged requirement in the review dashboard; for status questions post in the Shopify App Store forum category. Shopify says support tickets about status go to the same team.
escalate.draft: Our app <name> was submitted on <date> and has shown '<status>' since. Test credentials and the demo store are working. Is anything waiting on us?

checks.detail: Anyone with app development permissions or a Partner account creates apps in the Dev Dashboard and gets a client ID and secret at once.
Custom distribution reaches one outside merchant (or one Plus organisation) with no review; many merchants need a public app that passes App Store review.

Protected customer data (customers, orders, draft orders, fulfilment, gift cards) needs approval for public apps; some scopes need Shopify approval (e.g. read_all_orders, not in Composio's defaults); theme file edits need an exemption.
Public distribution requires App Store review, even at limited visibility. Custom distribution and own-store apps have no review.
No mandatory assessment or yearly re-verification. Shopify may select an app with protected customer data for a data protection review and ask for evidence.
A custom app serves one merchant (or one Plus organisation). A public app installs only on dev stores until approved.
A privacy policy and merchant agreement are required for custom and public apps. No legal-entity or domain verification found, but app URLs must not contain 'Shopify'.
Client and public apps need a Partner organisation; the App Store needs a one-time US$19 registration. Own-store apps need neither.
Draft public apps install only on dev stores, where protected data needs no review. Client credentials tokens last 24 hours; public apps' offline tokens last 1 hour with 90-day refresh tokens.
Shopify gives no review timeframe. Community reports: about 2 weeks in October 2026; around 2 months earlier in 2026.
Reply to reviewers per requirement in the review dashboard (App > Distribution); Partner Support for account issues; the Shopify developer forum.

unknowns.question: Does Composio's Shopify OAuth request expiring offline tokens (expiring=1)?
unknowns.why: New public apps can't call the GraphQL Admin API with non-expiring offline tokens. Composio says it refreshes tokens but doesn't say which token type it requests.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Connect a dev store to a public dev app through Composio and check whether the token response has an expiry, or ask Composio support.

unknowns.question: Can a Composio connection be started with the store name already filled in, so merchants never type it?
unknowns.why: App Store requirement 2.3.1 forbids asking for a shop domain during install or setup, and Composio's hosted connect form asks for it.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Initiate the connection from your server with the subdomain from Shopify's install request, and confirm the merchant goes straight to Shopify's grant screen.

unknowns.question: Does Shopify accept or reject read_webhooks and write_webhooks in Composio's default scopes?
unknowns.why: They are not in Shopify's scope references; an invalid scope could fail the release or the authorize step.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Remove both from the Dev Dashboard version and the Composio auth config, or test the default list once on a dev store.

unknowns.question: Do own-store and custom apps also need Shopify's exemption to edit theme files with write_themes?
unknowns.why: Shopify's API reference says modifying theme files needs an exemption without naming app types; if it applies, agents that edit themes face a product-access gate on every path.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Try a theme file update from a dev store app, or ask in the Shopify developer forum (Extensions).

unknowns.question: Must the client open the custom-distribution install link before Composio's connect flow works?
unknowns.why: Composio sends the merchant straight to the store's authorize URL; it is not documented whether that installs a custom-distribution app that hasn't been installed yet.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Test both orders on a dev store: Composio connect first, then install link first.

unknowns.question: How long does App Store review take right now?
unknowns.why: Shopify publishes no timeline; community reports range from about 2 weeks to about 2 months in 2026.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Check recent threads in the Shopify App Store category of community.shopify.dev before planning a launch date.

composio_notes.text: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify. You must create your own app and paste its client ID and secret.
Every connection needs the store's subdomain: only the store name (your-store-name), not your-store-name.myshopify.com and not a custom domain.
Register the exact callback your auth config uses. Composio warns that old or mistyped v1/v3 callback paths cause redirect failures, so copy the value shown in the dashboard.
For stores in your own organisation you can use Composio's S2S auth (Shopify's client credentials grant) instead of OAuth: no redirect, 24-hour tokens.
Composio refreshes tokens for custom Shopify credentials. A 400 during connection usually means a wrong client secret or a scope that needs Shopify's approval.
The toolkit is GraphQL-first but keeps legacy REST actions. New public apps must use only the GraphQL Admin API, so prefer the GraphQL tools.
Composio's default order scopes cover only the last 60 days of orders. Older orders need read_all_orders, which Shopify must approve.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.title: Store-level OpenID discovery (Shopify's Hydrogen demo store)
evidence.excerpt: HTTP 200; issuer https://shopify.com/authentication/55145660472; scopes_supported openid, email, customer-account-api:full (no Admin API scopes); no registration_endpoint; code_challenge_methods_supported: S256.
evidence.note: This is the Customer Account API (buyer login) server, not the Admin API OAuth used by Composio. /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server returned the same document.

probe.summary: Discovery exists but only for the Customer Account API; no registration_endpoint and no Admin API scopes or endpoints.

evidence.excerpt: HTTP 303 redirect to https://hydrogen-preview.myshopify.com/admin/auth/login?redirect=/admin/oauth/authorize?... (the endpoint lives on each store's own domain).

probe.summary: The Admin API authorize endpoint is served per store and sends unauthenticated users to the store's admin login.
